q: Dress Allowance introduced under the 7th CPC dispensation, in lieu of the erstwhile uniform-related allowances, is paid to the eligible railway servant:

options.A: Every month along with the salary
options.C: Only at the time of initial appointment

e: Dress Allowance, introduced under the 7th CPC in lieu of the erstwhile uniform-related allowances, is paid to the eligible railway servant once in a year.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Productivity Linked Bonus is admissible to non-gazetted railway employees other than RPF/RPSF personnel.
2. RPF/RPSF personnel are granted ad hoc bonus in lieu of Productivity Linked Bonus.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Productivity Linked Bonus is admissible to non-gazetted railway employees other than RPF/RPSF personnel, and RPF/RPSF personnel are granted ad hoc bonus in lieu of Productivity Linked Bonus.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. House Building Advance is admissible to a railway servant for construction of a house, as also for purchase of a ready-built house or flat.
2. House Building Advance can be drawn by a railway servant any number of times during his service.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: House Building Advance is admissible for construction of a house as well as for purchase of a ready-built house or flat. Statement 2 is wrong: the advance can be drawn only once during service.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A railway servant may become a member of a political party after obtaining permission from his controlling officer.
2. A railway servant shall not canvass, or otherwise intervene, in support of a candidate at an election to a legislature or a local authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is wrong: a railway servant cannot become a member of a political party at all. Statement 2 is correct: he shall not canvass, or otherwise intervene, in support of a candidate at an election to a legislature or local authority.

q: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, an applicant belonging to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category is:

options.A: Required to pay double the normal application fee
options.B: Required to pay the application fee in instalments
options.C: Exempt from payment of the application fee
options.D: Required to pay the application fee in full like other applicants

e: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, an applicant belonging to the Below Poverty Line category is exempt from payment of the application fee.

q: 'UMID' in the Railways refers to:

options.A: A system for online booking of retiring rooms
options.B: A software for preparation of salary bills
options.C: The portal for submission of pension papers
options.D: The Unique Medical Identity card issued to railway beneficiaries for availing medical facilities

e: 'UMID' refers to the Unique Medical Identity card issued to railway beneficiaries for availing medical facilities under the railway health scheme.

q: In regard to nomination for the General Provident Fund, the correct position is that:

options.A: A subscriber having a family may nominate any person, whether a member of his family or not
options.B: A subscriber who has no family may nominate any person; the nomination becomes invalid on his acquiring a family thereafter
options.C: Nomination can be made only in favour of the spouse
options.D: Nomination once made can never be cancelled or modified

e: A subscriber who has no family may nominate any person for the General Provident Fund, but such nomination becomes invalid on his acquiring a family thereafter; a subscriber having a family must nominate a family member.

q: A final (non-refundable) withdrawal from the General Provident Fund is ordinarily permissible to a subscriber only after he has completed:
e: A final (non-refundable) withdrawal from the General Provident Fund is ordinarily permissible to a subscriber only after he has completed 15 years of service.

q: Post-retirement complimentary passes are admissible to a retired railway servant who has rendered a minimum qualifying service of:
e: Post-retirement complimentary passes are admissible to a retired railway servant who has rendered a minimum qualifying service of 20 years.

q: A railway servant who joins service in the middle of a calendar half-year is credited with Leave on Average Pay for that half-year:

options.A: At the full rate of 15 days irrespective of the date of joining
options.B: At the rate of 2 days for each completed month of service in that half-year
options.C: Only with effect from the next half-year
options.D: At the rate of 2.5 days for each completed month of service in that half-year

e: A servant joining in the middle of a half-year is credited with Leave on Average Pay for that half-year at the rate of 2.5 days for each completed month of service, being the pro-rata of 15 days per half-year.

q: The maximum period of Leave Not Due that can be granted to a railway servant during his entire service is:
e: The maximum period of Leave Not Due that can be granted to a railway servant during his entire service is 360 days.

q: Extra Ordinary Leave can be granted to a railway servant at a time for a maximum period of:
e: Extra Ordinary Leave can be granted to a railway servant for a maximum period of 5 years at a time, in the special circumstances covered by the leave rules.

q: The leave salary admissible to a railway servant during a period of Special Disability Leave is:

options.A: Half pay throughout the period of the leave
options.B: Full pay throughout the period of the leave
options.C: Equal to the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay for the first 120 days, and equal to that admissible on Leave on Half Average Pay for the remaining period
options.D: No leave salary is admissible during Special Disability Leave

e: Leave salary during Special Disability Leave is equal to the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay for the first 120 days, and equal to that admissible on Leave on Half Average Pay for the remaining period.

q: The leave salary admissible to a railway servant during Leave on Half Average Pay is:

options.A: Equal to the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay
options.B: One-fourth of the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay
options.D: Half of the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay

e: Leave salary during Leave on Half Average Pay is half of the leave salary admissible on Leave on Average Pay.

q: Where a railway servant transferred in public interest does not avail the full joining time admissible to him, the unutilised portion of the joining time is:

options.A: Credited to his Leave on Average Pay account, subject to a maximum of 15 days
options.B: Credited to his Leave on Half Average Pay account, without any limit
options.D: Treated as lapsed in all circumstances

e: Where a railway servant transferred in public interest does not avail the full joining time, the unutilised portion is credited to his Leave on Average Pay account, subject to a maximum of 15 days.

q: The encashment of Leave on Average Pay availed of by a railway servant in conjunction with Leave Travel Concession during his entire service cannot exceed:
e: The encashment of Leave on Average Pay availed in conjunction with Leave Travel Concession during the entire service of a railway servant cannot exceed 60 days.

q: Encashment of Leave on Average Pay by a serving railway servant, otherwise than on his retirement or on his death in service, is admissible:

options.A: At any time on demand, once in a calendar year
options.C: Only for construction of a house
options.D: Only when he avails Leave Travel Concession

e: Encashment of Leave on Average Pay by a serving railway servant, otherwise than on retirement or death in service, is admissible only when he avails Leave Travel Concession.

q: Study leave is ordinarily admissible only to a railway servant who has completed a minimum service of:
e: Study leave is ordinarily admissible only to a railway servant who has completed a minimum service of 5 years.

q: Special Casual Leave admissible to a railway servant for participating in sporting events of national or international importance can be granted up to:
e: Special Casual Leave for participating in sporting events of national or international importance can be granted up to 30 days in a calendar year.

q: The age of superannuation for a railway servant, other than the categories for which a different age is specially prescribed, is:
e: The age of superannuation for a railway servant is 60 years, except for the categories for which a different age is specially prescribed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A railway servant retiring voluntarily from service is given a weightage of up to five years in his qualifying service for the purpose of pension.
2. The total qualifying service, after adding such weightage, shall not exceed 33 years and the weightage shall not take him beyond the date of his normal superannuation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: a voluntarily retiring servant gets a weightage of up to five years in qualifying service, but the total qualifying service after weightage cannot exceed 33 years nor go beyond the normal superannuation date.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Resignation from service by a railway servant ordinarily entails forfeiture of his past service for the purpose of pension.
2. Where the resignation is a 'technical resignation', tendered to take up another appointment under the Government with proper permission, the past service is not forfeited and counts for pension in the new service.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: resignation ordinarily entails forfeiture of past service for pension, but a technical resignation tendered with proper permission to join another Government appointment does not forfeit the past service.

q: For the purpose of pension, a fraction of a year in the qualifying service of a railway servant is treated as one completed six-monthly period if it is equal to:
e: For the purpose of pension, a fraction of a year in qualifying service equal to 3 months or more is treated as one completed six-monthly period.

q: A railway servant dies in service after completing 8 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 45,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family is:
e: For qualifying service of 5 years or more but less than 11 years, death gratuity is 12 times the emoluments: 12 x Rs 45,000 = Rs 5,40,000.

q: 'Average emoluments', for the purpose of computing the pension of a railway servant, means the average of the emoluments drawn by him during:

options.A: The last 10 months of his service
options.B: The last 12 months of his service
options.C: The last 3 years of his service
options.D: The entire period of his qualifying service

e: 'Average emoluments' for computing pension means the average of the emoluments drawn by the railway servant during the last 10 months of his service.

q: Compensation pension is admissible to a railway servant when he:

options.A: Retires on attaining the age of superannuation
options.B: Is removed from service on account of misconduct
options.C: Is discharged owing to the abolition of his permanent post
options.D: Resigns from service of his own accord

e: Compensation pension is admissible to a railway servant when he is discharged owing to the abolition of his permanent post.

q: Verification of the service of a railway servant for pension purposes is carried out, and a certificate of the qualifying service rendered by him is issued to him, after he completes:
e: Verification of a railway servant's service for pension purposes is carried out, and a certificate of the qualifying service rendered is issued to him, after he completes 25 years of service.

q: A railway pensioner's monthly pension is Rs 30,000. He commutes 40% of his pension. Taking the commutation factor for his age on the next birthday (61 years) as 8.194, the lump sum commuted value payable to him is:
e: Commuted portion = 40% of Rs 30,000 = Rs 12,000 per month; lump sum = 12,000 x 8.194 x 12 = Rs 11,79,936.

q: Recovery of House Building Advance granted to a railway servant is effected in a maximum of:

options.A: 120 monthly instalments, all towards the principal
options.C: 180 monthly instalments, the first 156 instalments being towards the principal and the remaining 24 towards interest

e: Recovery of House Building Advance is effected in a maximum of 180 monthly instalments, the first 156 instalments being towards the principal and the remaining 24 towards interest.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 60,000 per month applies for House Building Advance for construction of a house. The maximum amount of advance admissible to him is:
e: Maximum House Building Advance is 139 times the monthly basic pay: 139 x Rs 60,000 = Rs 83,40,000, which is within the overall ceiling of Rs 1 crore.

q: A final (non-refundable) withdrawal by a railway servant from the balance at his credit in the General Provident Fund is ordinarily limited to:

options.A: 50% of the balance at his credit
options.B: 60% of the balance at his credit
options.C: 90% of the balance at his credit
options.D: 75% of the balance at his credit

e: A final (non-refundable) withdrawal from the General Provident Fund is ordinarily limited to 75% of the balance at the credit of the subscriber.

q: A temporary (refundable) advance from the Provident Fund is ordinarily admissible to a railway servant to meet expenditure in connection with:

options.A: Purchase of consumer durables for his household
options.B: The illness and medical treatment of himself, or of a member of his family dependent on him

e: A temporary (refundable) advance from the Provident Fund is ordinarily admissible to meet expenditure in connection with the illness and medical treatment of the railway servant himself, or of a member of his family dependent on him.

q: A subscriber who exits from the National Pension System prematurely, before attaining the age of 60 years, is required to utilise for the purchase of an annuity at least:
e: A subscriber who exits from the National Pension System prematurely, before attaining the age of 60 years, must utilise at least 80% of the accumulated pension wealth for the purchase of an annuity.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the assured payout on superannuation of a railway servant who has rendered a qualifying service of 25 years or more is:

options.A: 50% of the basic pay drawn in the last month of service
options.B: 60% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months
options.C: 50% of the average basic pay drawn during the last 12 months immediately prior to superannuation
options.D: 40% of the average basic pay of the last 10 months

e: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the assured payout on superannuation with a qualifying service of 25 years or more is 50% of the average basic pay drawn during the last 12 months immediately prior to superannuation.

q: Under the National Pension System, the railway servant's own monthly contribution to his Tier-I account is:

options.A: 14% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.B: 12% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.C: 8% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.D: 10% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance

e: Under the National Pension System, the railway servant's own monthly contribution to his Tier-I account is 10% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Children Education Allowance is admissible in respect of all the surviving children of a railway servant, without any limit on their number.
2. Children Education Allowance in respect of a Divyang (differently abled) child is reimbursed at double the normal rate.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is wrong: Children Education Allowance is admissible only for the two eldest surviving children. Statement 2 is correct: in respect of a Divyang child, the allowance is reimbursed at double the normal rate.

q: A railway servant on tour remains absent from his headquarters for more than 12 hours in a day. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for that day is:
e: Where a railway servant on tour is absent from his headquarters for more than 12 hours in a day, the full (100%) admissible rate of Daily Allowance is payable for that day.

q: A Group 'C' railway servant who has completed more than five years of service is entitled to privilege passes in a calendar year up to:
e: A Group 'C' railway servant who has completed more than five years of service is entitled to 3 sets of privilege passes in a calendar year.

q: Deputation (Duty) Allowance admissible to a railway servant on deputation to an ex-cadre post is payable at the rate of:

options.A: 5% of basic pay, whether the deputation is within the same station or involves a change of station
options.B: 10% of basic pay in all cases
options.C: 2.5% of basic pay within the same station and 5% of basic pay on change of station
options.D: 5% of basic pay where the deputation is within the same station, and 10% of basic pay where it involves a change of station

e: Deputation (Duty) Allowance is payable at 5% of basic pay where the deputation is within the same station, and at 10% of basic pay where it involves a change of station.

q: Transport Allowance is NOT admissible to a railway servant for a month in which he:

options.A: Avails casual leave for a few days
options.B: Remains absent from duty for the whole calendar month, for example on leave or under suspension
options.C: Is posted to a station classified in a lower category
options.D: Proceeds on tour for a part of the month

e: Transport Allowance is not admissible to a railway servant for a month in which he remains absent from duty for the whole calendar month, for example on leave or under suspension.

q: 'Withholding of increments of pay without cumulative effect' is classified under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules as:

options.D: A penalty imposable only by the Railway Board

e: 'Withholding of increments of pay without cumulative effect' is classified as a minor penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules; the same penalty with cumulative effect is a major penalty.

q: 'Reduction to a lower time scale of pay, grade, post or service' is classified under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules as:

options.B: An administrative action, and not a penalty
options.D: A penalty that can be imposed without holding an inquiry in all cases

e: 'Reduction to a lower time scale of pay, grade, post or service' involves a lasting loss to the railway servant and is classified as a major penalty under the Discipline and Appeal Rules.

q: Under Article 311(1) of the Constitution, a railway servant shall not be dismissed or removed from service by an authority:

options.A: Which is not his controlling officer
options.B: Which has not held a departmental inquiry
options.C: Of a rank lower than the General Manager of the Railway
options.D: Subordinate to the authority by which he was appointed

e: Under Article 311(1) of the Constitution, a railway servant shall not be dismissed or removed from service by an authority subordinate to the authority by which he was appointed.

q: Where an inquiry has been held in a major penalty case under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the disciplinary authority, before passing final orders, shall:

options.A: Forward the case to the Union Public Service Commission in every case
options.B: Supply a copy of the report of the Inquiring Authority to the charged railway servant and give him an opportunity to submit his representation against the findings
options.C: Hold a fresh inquiry through another Inquiring Authority
options.D: Obtain the prior approval of the Railway Board in every case

e: After an inquiry in a major penalty case, the disciplinary authority must supply a copy of the Inquiring Authority's report to the charged railway servant and give him an opportunity to submit his representation against the findings before passing final orders.

q: When a railway servant who was under suspension is reinstated in service, the pay and allowances payable to him for the period of suspension, and whether that period shall be treated as duty, are determined:

options.A: By a specific order of the competent authority, full pay and allowances being admissible where the suspension is held to have been wholly unjustified
options.B: Automatically, the period being always treated as duty with full pay
options.C: By the Accounts Office, on the basis of the muster roll
options.D: Only by the Railway Board, in every case

e: On reinstatement after suspension, the pay and allowances for the suspension period, and whether it counts as duty, are decided by a specific order of the competent authority; full pay is admissible where the suspension is held to have been wholly unjustified.

q: The 'sealed cover procedure', in matters of promotion of railway servants, refers to:

options.A: Sealing the question papers of the selection examination till the date of the examination
options.B: Keeping the seniority list in a sealed cover till its publication
options.C: Placing the recommendations of the Departmental Promotion Committee in respect of a railway servant who is under suspension, or against whom disciplinary or criminal proceedings are pending, in a sealed cover, to be acted upon after the conclusion of the proceedings
options.D: Forwarding the APAR dossier of the railway servant to the Railway Board in a sealed cover

e: Under the sealed cover procedure, the Departmental Promotion Committee's recommendations for a servant under suspension, or facing disciplinary or criminal proceedings, are kept in a sealed cover and acted upon only after the proceedings conclude.

q: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, where the information sought concerns the life or liberty of a person, it shall be provided within:

options.A: 30 days of the receipt of the request
options.B: 15 days of the receipt of the request
options.C: 7 days of the receipt of the request
options.D: 48 hours of the receipt of the request

e: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, where the information sought concerns the life or liberty of a person, it shall be provided within 48 hours of the receipt of the request.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not, in connection with any matter pertaining to his own service or the service of any other railway servant:

options.A: Approach his superior officer with a representation
options.B: Engage in any demonstration, or resort to any form of strike, coercion or physical duress
options.C: Become a member of a recognised trade union
options.D: Submit a memorial to the President of India

e: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not engage in any demonstration, or resort to any form of strike, coercion or physical duress, in connection with any matter pertaining to his own service or that of another railway servant.

q: The Annual Immovable Property Return for a calendar year is required to be submitted by gazetted railway officers (Group 'A' and Group 'B') by:
e: The Annual Immovable Property Return for a calendar year is required to be submitted by gazetted railway officers (Group 'A' and Group 'B') by 31st January of the following year.

q: 'Honorarium' payable to a railway servant means:

options.A: A payment received by him from a source other than the general revenues of the Government
options.B: A monthly payment made to retired railway servants
options.C: A recurring or non-recurring payment granted to him from the general revenues in remuneration for work of a special nature, of an occasional or intermittent character
options.D: A payment made only to part-time employees of the Railways

e: 'Honorarium' is a recurring or non-recurring payment granted to a railway servant from the general revenues in remuneration for work of a special nature, of an occasional or intermittent character.

q: Reservation in promotion on the Railways is admissible for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, respectively, at:
e: Reservation in promotion on the Railways is admissible for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes at 15% and 7.5% respectively.

q: Creation of new posts on the Railways is normally permitted only against:

options.A: Fresh budgetary provision in the Works Programme
options.B: Matching surrender of posts of equivalent value (matching savings)
options.C: Approval of the Railway Recruitment Board
options.D: Savings surrendered from the Stores Budget

e: Creation of new posts on the Railways is normally permitted only against matching surrender of posts of equivalent value, i.e., matching savings.

q: A railway servant who is prematurely retired in public interest under the relevant retirement rules is entitled to:

options.A: A notice of not less than three months, or pay and allowances in lieu of such notice
options.B: A notice of one month only
options.C: No notice, as the retirement is ordered in public interest
options.D: A notice of six months in all cases

e: A railway servant prematurely retired in public interest under the relevant retirement rules is entitled to a notice of not less than three months, or pay and allowances in lieu of such notice.

q: A candidate is appointed to a post on the Railways on 10th August, 2026. He will draw his first annual increment on:
e: Under the 7th CPC, annual increments fall on 1st January or 1st July; a person appointed on 10th August, 2026 (between 2nd July and 1st January) draws his first increment on 1st July, 2027.

q: Family pension is admissible to the dependent parents of a deceased railway servant when:

options.A: The railway servant is survived by a widow and children
options.B: The parents were not dependent on the railway servant
options.C: The deceased railway servant has not left behind a widow or widower or a child, and the parents were wholly dependent on him when he was alive
options.D: The parents attain the age of 80 years

e: Family pension is admissible to the dependent parents only when the deceased railway servant has left behind no widow, widower or child, and the parents were wholly dependent on him when he was alive.

q: Leave on Half Average Pay is credited in advance to the leave account of a railway servant in two instalments of 10 days each, falling due on:
e: Leave on Half Average Pay is credited in advance in two instalments of 10 days each, falling due on 1st January and 1st July.

q: Child Care Leave cannot be granted to a railway servant in more than the following number of spells in a calendar year:
e: Child Care Leave cannot be granted to a railway servant in more than three spells in a calendar year.

q: The leave salary admissible to a railway servant during Child Care Leave is:

options.A: 80% of leave salary for the first 365 days and 100% for the remaining period
options.B: 100% of leave salary for the first 365 days and nil for the remaining period
options.C: 50% of leave salary throughout the entire period
options.D: 100% of leave salary for the first 365 days and 80% of leave salary for the remaining 365 days

e: Leave salary during Child Care Leave is 100% of the leave salary for the first 365 days and 80% of the leave salary for the remaining 365 days.

q: Child Care Leave is admissible to a single male railway servant, such as a widower or a divorcee having minor children:

options.A: Not admissible; the leave is admissible only to female railway servants
options.B: Admissible only if he has completed 20 years of service
options.C: Admissible, for taking care of his two eldest surviving minor children
options.D: Admissible only with the personal sanction of the Railway Board

e: Child Care Leave is admissible to a single male railway servant, such as a widower or a divorcee having minor children, for taking care of his two eldest surviving minor children.

q: Work Related Illness and Injury Leave (WRIIL), admissible to a railway servant who is hospitalised on account of an illness or injury attributable to his duty, carries, for the period of hospitalisation, leave salary equal to:

options.C: The leave salary admissible on Leave on Half Average Pay
options.D: No leave salary is payable during such leave

e: Work Related Illness and Injury Leave, admissible on hospitalisation for an illness or injury attributable to duty, carries leave salary equal to full pay for the period of hospitalisation.

q: A railway servant is transferred in public interest to a station involving a journey of about 1,500 kilometres. The joining time admissible to him is:
e: Joining time is graded according to the distance involved in the transfer; for a journey of about 1,500 kilometres, the joining time admissible is 12 days.

q: Where a railway servant is transferred from one post to another at the same station, the joining time admissible to him is:
e: Where a railway servant is transferred from one post to another at the same station, the joining time admissible to him is one day.

q: While availing encashment of Leave on Average Pay in conjunction with Leave Travel Concession, the minimum balance of Leave on Average Pay that must remain at the credit of the railway servant after such encashment is:
e: While availing encashment of Leave on Average Pay in conjunction with Leave Travel Concession, a minimum balance of 30 days of Leave on Average Pay must remain at the credit of the railway servant after the encashment.

q: Casual leave admissible to a railway servant:

options.A: Is debited to his leave account
options.B: May be availed of for half a day also
options.C: Can be combined with Leave on Average Pay
options.D: Can be accumulated and carried forward to the next calendar year

e: Casual leave is not debited to the leave account, cannot be combined with other leave and cannot be accumulated, but it may be availed of for half a day also.

q: The instalments of Dearness Allowance admissible to railway servants are ordinarily made effective from:

options.A: 1st April and 1st October of each year
options.B: 1st March and 1st September of each year
options.C: The date of issue of the orders in each case
options.D: 1st January and 1st July of each year

e: The instalments of Dearness Allowance admissible to railway servants are ordinarily made effective from 1st January and 1st July of each year.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the option to be exercised by a railway servant for fixation of pay on promotion:
1. The option is to be exercised within one month from the date of promotion.
2. The option, once exercised, is final.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the option for fixation of pay on promotion is to be exercised within one month from the date of promotion, and the option once exercised is final.

q: The pay of a railway servant appointed by direct recruitment to a post on or after 01.01.2016 is, in the normal course, fixed:

options.A: At the first cell, i.e., the minimum, of the level of the post
options.B: Two cells above the minimum of the level of the post
options.C: At any cell of the level chosen by the appointing authority
options.D: At the maximum of the level of the post

e: The pay of a railway servant appointed by direct recruitment to a post on or after 01.01.2016 is, in the normal course, fixed at the first cell, i.e., the minimum, of the level of the post.

q: Stepping up of pay of a senior railway servant with reference to a junior railway servant who draws higher pay solely on account of grant of financial upgradation under the MACP scheme:

options.A: Is admissible as a matter of right
options.B: Is admissible if both belong to the same cadre
options.C: Is admissible with the sanction of the General Manager

e: Stepping up of pay of a senior with reference to a junior who draws higher pay solely on account of financial upgradation under the MACP scheme is not admissible.

q: For the purpose of computing Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity, the 'emoluments' reckoned are:

options.B: Basic pay plus the Dearness Allowance admissible on the relevant date
options.C: Basic pay plus all allowances drawn by the railway servant
options.D: Basic pay plus House Rent Allowance only

e: For the purpose of computing Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity, the 'emoluments' reckoned are the basic pay plus the Dearness Allowance admissible on the relevant date.

q: Retirement gratuity is admissible to a railway servant only if he has completed a minimum qualifying service of:
e: Retirement gratuity is admissible to a railway servant only if he has completed a minimum qualifying service of 5 years.

q: A railway servant dies in service after rendering nine months of qualifying service. The death gratuity payable to his family is:

options.D: Not admissible, as the minimum qualifying service is not completed

e: For qualifying service of less than one year, the death gratuity payable to the family of the deceased railway servant is 2 times his emoluments.

q: Where a deceased railway servant has made no nomination for gratuity, or no valid nomination subsists, the gratuity is paid:

options.A: Only to his widow or widower
options.D: To the members of his family in equal shares

e: Where the deceased railway servant has made no nomination for gratuity, or no valid nomination subsists, the gratuity is paid to the members of his family in equal shares.

q: The minimum amount of family pension admissible under the 7th CPC dispensation is:
e: The minimum amount of family pension admissible under the 7th CPC dispensation is Rs 9,000 per month.

q: The maximum amount of pension admissible to a railway pensioner under the 7th CPC dispensation is:
e: The maximum amount of pension admissible to a railway pensioner under the 7th CPC dispensation is Rs 1,25,000 per month.

q: The additional quantum of pension admissible to a railway pensioner on attaining the age of 90 years is:
e: The additional quantum of pension admissible to a railway pensioner on attaining the age of 90 years is 40% of the basic pension.

q: The basic pension of a railway pensioner who retired before 01.01.2016 was revised, under one of the prescribed methods of revision, by multiplying the existing basic pension by a fitment factor of:
e: The basic pension of a pre-01.01.2016 pensioner was revised, under one of the prescribed methods, by multiplying the existing basic pension by a fitment factor of 2.57.

q: A railway pensioner is required to furnish a life certificate to the pension disbursing authority once a year, in the month of:
e: A railway pensioner is required to furnish a life certificate to the pension disbursing authority once a year, in the month of November.

q: 'Jeevan Pramaan' is:

options.A: The digital pension payment order issued to a new pensioner
options.B: A health insurance scheme for railway pensioners
options.C: A biometric-enabled digital life certificate for pensioners
options.D: A portal for lodging pension grievances

e: 'Jeevan Pramaan' is a biometric-enabled digital life certificate for pensioners, which dispenses with the need for the pensioner to be physically present before the disbursing authority.

q: The online portal used on the Indian Railways for submission and processing of the pension revision cases of railway pensioners is:
e: ARPAN is the online portal used on the Indian Railways for submission and processing of the pension revision cases of railway pensioners.

q: Dearness Relief admissible to a railway pensioner is calculated:

options.A: On the reduced pension only, after deducting the portion commuted by him
options.B: Only on 60% of the basic pension
options.C: On the basic pension excluding the additional quantum of pension
options.D: On the full basic pension, including the portion of pension commuted by him

e: Dearness Relief to a railway pensioner is calculated on the full basic pension, including the portion of pension commuted by him, and not merely on the reduced pension.

q: Family pension payable to the widow of a deceased railway servant continues until:

options.A: She attains the age of 60 years
options.B: Her death or remarriage, whichever is earlier
options.C: A maximum period of 30 years from the date of death
options.D: Her eldest son starts earning his livelihood

e: Family pension payable to the widow of a deceased railway servant continues until her death or remarriage, whichever is earlier.

q: The ex-gratia lump sum compensation payable to the family of a railway servant who dies in the course of duty is:

options.A: Payable in lieu of family pension
options.B: Adjusted against the death gratuity payable to the family
options.C: Payable in addition to family pension, death gratuity and other pensionary benefits
options.D: Admissible only where no family pension is payable

e: The ex-gratia lump sum compensation payable to the family of a railway servant who dies in the course of duty is payable in addition to family pension, death gratuity and other pensionary benefits.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the contribution of the Government to the individual corpus of the subscriber is at the rate of:

options.A: 18.5% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.B: 10% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.C: 14% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.D: 24% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance

e: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the contribution of the Government to the individual corpus of the subscriber is at the rate of 18.5% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding partial withdrawal from the National Pension System:
1. Partial withdrawal from the Tier-I account is permissible only after completion of three years from the opening of the account.
2. Such withdrawal is admissible for purposes such as higher education or marriage of children, purchase or construction of a residential house, and medical treatment of specified illnesses.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: partial withdrawal from the NPS Tier-I account is permissible only after three years from the opening of the account, and it is admissible for purposes like children's higher education or marriage, house purchase or construction, and medical treatment of specified illnesses.

q: A railway servant who retires on invalid pension and applies for commutation of a portion of his pension:

options.A: Is not required to undergo medical examination in any case
options.B: Can commute a portion of his pension only after medical examination by the competent medical authority
options.C: Cannot commute any portion of his pension
options.D: Can commute up to 50% of his pension without any medical examination

e: A railway servant who retires on invalid pension can commute a portion of his pension only after medical examination by the competent medical authority.

q: A railway servant compulsorily retired from service as a measure of penalty is entitled to pension and gratuity at a rate:

options.A: Not less than two-thirds and not more than the full amount of the pension or gratuity which would have been admissible to him had he retired on a compensation pension
options.B: Equal to the full compensation pension in all cases
options.C: Equal to one-half of the compensation pension in all cases
options.D: No pension or gratuity is admissible to him in any case

e: A railway servant compulsorily retired as a measure of penalty is entitled to pension and gratuity at a rate not less than two-thirds and not more than the full amount admissible had he retired on a compensation pension.

q: The period of probation prescribed for a railway servant appointed by direct recruitment to a non-gazetted post is ordinarily:
e: The period of probation prescribed for a railway servant appointed by direct recruitment to a non-gazetted post is ordinarily two years.

q: The services of a temporary railway servant may be terminated by either side by giving a notice of:

options.C: One calendar month, or pay in lieu thereof

e: The services of a temporary railway servant may be terminated by either side by giving a notice of one calendar month, or pay in lieu thereof.

q: The order placing a railway servant under suspension is issued in Standard Form:
e: The order placing a railway servant under suspension is issued in Standard Form SF-1.

q: The memorandum for imposition of a minor penalty on a railway servant is issued in Standard Form:
e: The memorandum for imposition of a minor penalty on a railway servant is issued in Standard Form SF-11.

q: The fee prescribed for making an application seeking information under the Right to Information Act, 2005 is:
e: The fee prescribed for making an application seeking information under the Right to Information Act, 2005 is Rs 10.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant who has a spouse living:

options.A: May enter into another marriage freely if his personal law permits it
options.B: May enter into another marriage after merely informing his controlling officer
options.C: Shall not enter into another marriage, except with the previous permission of the Government where such a marriage is permissible under the personal law applicable to him
options.D: May enter into another marriage only after his retirement

e: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant who has a spouse living shall not enter into another marriage, except with the previous permission of the Government where such a marriage is permissible under his personal law.

q: A railway servant is required to report to the prescribed authority a transaction in movable property entered into by him, where the value of the transaction exceeds:
e: A railway servant is required to report to the prescribed authority a transaction in movable property entered into by him where the value of the transaction exceeds two months' basic pay.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant is prohibited from:

options.A: Making a statement of fact or opinion in a radio broadcast, a communication to the press or a published document, which has the effect of an adverse criticism of any current or recent policy of the Central or a State Government
options.B: Becoming a member of a recognised service association
options.C: Exercising his vote in a general election
options.D: Publishing a work of a purely literary, artistic or scientific character

e: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant is prohibited from making a statement of fact or opinion in a radio broadcast, press communication or published document which has the effect of an adverse criticism of any current or recent policy of the Central or a State Government.

q: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, staff whose duties are of a supervisory or confidential nature and who are not governed by the prescribed rostered hours of work are classified as:
e: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, staff whose duties are of a supervisory or confidential nature and who are not governed by the prescribed rostered hours of work are classified as 'Excluded'.

q: Staff classified as 'Essentially Intermittent' under the Hours of Employment Regulations are entitled to a period of rest in a week of not less than:

options.A: 30 consecutive hours including one full night
options.B: 36 consecutive hours including one full night
options.C: 24 consecutive hours including one full night
options.D: 24 consecutive hours, with no condition regarding a full night

e: Staff classified as 'Essentially Intermittent' under the Hours of Employment Regulations are entitled to a period of rest in a week of not less than 24 consecutive hours including one full night.

q: The monthly subscription payable by a Group 'C' railway servant under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme is:
e: The monthly subscription payable by a Group 'C' railway servant under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme is Rs 30 per month.

q: The amount of insurance cover admissible to the family of a Group 'C' railway servant who dies in service, under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, is:
e: The amount of insurance cover admissible to the family of a Group 'C' railway servant who dies in service under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme is Rs 30,000.

q: The one-time contribution payable by a retiring railway servant for joining the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme (RELHS) is equal to:

options.A: Two months' basic pay last drawn by him
options.C: Six months' basic pay last drawn by him
options.D: One month's basic pay last drawn by him

e: The one-time contribution payable by a retiring railway servant for joining the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme is equal to one month's basic pay last drawn by him.

q: National Holiday Allowance is admissible to:

options.A: All railway servants, whether or not they are on duty on the national holiday
options.B: Only gazetted officers who attend office on a national holiday
options.C: Only running staff working trains on a national holiday
options.D: Eligible non-gazetted railway servants who are required to perform duty on a national holiday

e: National Holiday Allowance is admissible to eligible non-gazetted railway servants who are required to perform duty on a national holiday.
